Singapore has many tourist attractions. Some of these are shown in Fig. 1.3 (Insert).

The students decided to investigate the following hypotheses:
Hypothesis 1: Most tourists to Singapore come from Europe.
Hypothesis 2: People in different age groups prefer to visit different attractions in Singapore.

in Singapore, the students asked 20 tourists in each age group to rank the five attractions
they most like (question 3 in the questionnaire). The results for the under 20 age group are

text: Students from a school in Singapore, a country in Southeast Asia, were studying tourism. Tourism
is an important industry in Singapore. It contributes about 10% of the country’s GDP (annual
income) and employs more than one million workers.

The students decided to investigate the following hypotheses:
Hypothesis 1: River discharge increases downstream.
Hypothesis 2: River meanders become larger downstream.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Which is the correct definition of river discharge? Tick (3) your answer.
tick (3)
The largest size of rocks a river can transport at a particular point in its course.
The volume of water which flows through a river channel in a given time.
The speed at which water flows along a river in a straight line.
The maximum amount of load a river can carry at a particular point in its course.

To calculate river discharge at each site the students needed to measure river velocity and
find out the area of the river cross-section.

parts.text: Describe a fieldwork method used to measure river velocity.
